decision.coverage: Eight LB questions, both seeds and two engine repeats satisfy the minimum exposure/coverage condition if all complete scope counts equal32. RULER is reported separately.
decision.deployable_headroom: No >=10% request-latency benefit established by this factorial audit. See separate clean headroom/profile review; its audit trajectories differ from clean and critical-path transfer is unresolved.
decision.mechanism_triage: Future-support preservation under sparse current output is the stronger follow-up hypothesis: repeated adverse score changes, positive N cost of holding across seeds/engines/leave-one-question-out. It is not a qualified deployable selector or a proof of universal dense-output necessity.
decision.reason: Observed A/A N/hash drift and same-arm engine-repeat drift prevent an unconditional clean causal or exact reproducibility claim. Current-output conditional effects also fail seed and leave-one-question-out stability. The frozen rule did not specify a statistical noise estimator; reporting mean-noise and maximum excursions avoids silently choosing a permissive interpretation.
decision.required_next_step: Resolve repeatability and qualify a useful regime before promoting selector engineering or serving-speed claims. Retain the inherited V31 and fixed refresh as baselines.
decision.structural_vs_causal: Frozen summary passed prefix/integrity gates describe recorded checks; they do not override the A/A comparability gate or imply cloned full-engine state.

limitations: Previously examined bounded prompts; eight LB question clusters do not estimate full-benchmark accuracy.
Engine repeats remain in question-cluster bootstrap and are not independent accuracy samples.
All opposite-direction and tail cases are retained; no nonsignificance implies noninferiority.
CURRENT output uses the common old mask; FUTURE map is exact fresh versus held. This is not fresh-mask sparse output at the same event.
First-event intervention is not a test of replacing every refresh, initialization, or commit.
The frozen summary uses generic full-state prefix wording; only the measured recorded prefix/first-GLOBAL fingerprint scope is justified.
RULER scorer values are partial-credit task scores on0–1 scale; .875 is not necessarily7/8 fully correct.
No numerical wall-time comparison from factorial instrumented rows is interpreted as speedup.
scope: Bounded first-progress-event mechanism diagnostic; audit time is not deployable latency. No cheap selector is tested.
